title: Cinnamon Swirl Focaccia with Vanilla Glaze
changes_from_base: Plain-flour dough with cinnamon butter folded through and swirled on top, finished with a vanilla glaze.
summary: Focaccia streaked with cinnamon butter, caramelised in the dimples and drizzled with a vanilla glaze, like a cinnamon roll in a tin.
equipment: cling film or a clean tea towel

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Whisk the flour, salt, yeast and caster sugar, add the warm water and 1.5 tbsp oil and stir until completely smooth. Cover for 15 min.

steps.title: Cinnamon butter
steps.text: Mash the brown sugar, soft butter and cinnamon into a paste.

steps.title: Folds
steps.text: Give the dough four sets of bowl folds 15 min apart; before the third and fourth sets, dot a teaspoon or two of the cinnamon butter over the dough so it gets folded into streaks. Cover and leave about 1 1/2 h, until doubled.

steps.title: Tin
steps.text: Oil the tin with 2 tbsp oil, turn the dough into it and coax it to the corners. Cover and leave 45-60 min, until puffy.

steps.title: Swirl
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan). Drizzle the last 1 tbsp oil, dimple deeply, then spoon the remaining cinnamon butter into the hollows and swirl it with a fingertip. Bake 22-25 min, until golden and bubbling; the centre reads about 96 °C. The sugar melts into the dimples and caramelises at the edges.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Stir the icing sugar, milk, vanilla and pinch of salt until smooth. Cool the focaccia 15 min, drizzle with the glaze and cut into 12.

tips: Keep the cinnamon butter soft so it spreads into the dimples easily.
Glaze the bread warm, not hot, or the glaze melts away.
A common mistake is under-proofing; the dough should be very puffy before baking.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for up to 2 days. Warm at 160 °C for 5 min; freeze unglazed for up to 1 month.
